
##adegenet dapc notes

```{r}

rm(list=ls())
library(adegenet)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)
library(DataCombine)

#read in genotype data
geno<-read.delim("/Users/erincollins/Google Drive/My Drive/Erin's Projects/Chipps_DAPC/cv_juv_ikaln_cutoff_snp_panel.IBSonly.sites_hatcheries_added.txt", colClasses = "character", header = F)
#combine chr and loci columns
geno$V1 <- paste(geno$V1,geno$V2)
#transpose the data, while keeping headers
genot <- setNames(data.frame(t(geno[,-1])), geno[,1])
names(genot) <- sub(" ", "_", names(genot))
#remove "." from loci names
names(genot) <- gsub("\\.", "", names(genot))
#column with metadata
meta <- select(genot, chr_pos)

```

```{r}

#parse dataframes by genotypes to add accurate loci, then recombine later
genotAC.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "A" & genot[3, ] == "C"]
genotAC.1[genotAC.1 == "1"] <- "A"
genotAC.2<-genotAC.1
genotAC.2[genotAC.2 == "0"] <- "C"
genotAG.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "A" & genot[3, ] == "G"]
genotAG.1[genotAG.1 == "1"] <- "A"
genotAG.2<-genotAG.1
genotAG.2[genotAG.2 == "0"] <- "G"
genotAT.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "A" & genot[3, ] == "T"]
genotAT.1[genotAT.1 == "1"] <- "A"
genotAT.2<-genotAT.1
genotAT.2[genotAT.2 == "0"] <- "T"
genotCA.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "C" & genot[3, ] == "A"]
genotCA.1[genotCA.1 == "1"] <- "C"
genotCA.2<-genotCA.1
genotCA.2[genotCA.2 == "0"] <- "A"
genotCG.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "C" & genot[3, ] == "G"]
genotCG.1[genotCG.1 == "1"] <- "C"
genotCG.2<-genotCG.1
genotCG.2[genotCG.2 == "0"] <- "G"
genotCT.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "C" & genot[3, ] == "T"]
genotCT.1[genotCT.1 == "1"] <- "C"
genotCT.2<-genotCT.1
genotCT.2[genotCT.2 == "0"] <- "T"
genotGA.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "G" & genot[3, ] == "A"]
genotGA.1[genotGA.1 == "1"] <- "G"
genotGA.2<-genotGA.1
genotGA.2[genotGA.2 == "0"] <- "A"
genotGC.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "G" & genot[3, ] == "C"]
genotGC.1[genotGC.1 == "1"] <- "G"
genotGC.2<-genotGC.1
genotGC.2[genotGC.2 == "0"] <- "C"
genotGT.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "G" & genot[3, ] == "T"]
genotGT.1[genotGT.1 == "1"] <- "G"
genotGT.2<-genotGT.1
genotGT.2[genotGT.2 == "0"] <- "T"
genotTA.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "T" & genot[3, ] == "A"]
genotTA.1[genotTA.1 == "1"] <- "T"
genotTA.2<-genotTA.1
genotTA.2[genotTA.2 == "0"] <- "A"
genotTC.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "T" & genot[3, ] == "C"]
genotTC.1[genotTC.1 == "1"] <- "T"
genotTC.2<-genotTC.1
genotTC.2[genotTC.2 == "0"] <- "C"
genotTG.1 <- genot[, genot[2, ] == "T" & genot[3, ] == "G"]
genotTG.1[genotTG.1 == "1"] <- "T"
genotTG.2<-genotTG.1
genotTG.2[genotTG.2 == "0"] <- "G"

#recombine reformatted columns and metadata
genot.1<-cbind(meta,genotAC.2,genotAG.2,genotAT.2,genotCA.2,genotCG.2,genotCT.2,genotGA.2,genotGC.2,genotGT.2,genotTA.2,genotTC.2,genotTG.2)
#remove chromosome, major, and minor rows
genot.2 <- genot.1[-(1:3),]


# Use Tasha's Sup.Table 1 for filtering, used fall guidelines because all assigned to fall

#### REMOVES SAMPLES with > 80% missing data ###

genot.2[genot.2 == -1] <- NA

#only keep individuals if 97% missing, remove individuals if >97% missing
filtered_samples <- genot.2[which(rowMeans(!is.na(genot.2)) > 0.03),]
removed_samples <- genot.2[which(rowMeans(!is.na(genot.2)) < 0.03),]

#only keep individuals if 80% missing, remove individuals if >80% missing
filtered_samples.1 <- filtered_samples[which(rowMeans(!is.na(filtered_samples)) > 0.2),]
removed_samples.1 <- removed_samples[which(rowMeans(!is.na(removed_samples)) < 0.2),]

#checked and the threshold for >80%, same samples are retained, thus fall vs. late-fall assignments are reliable 

# filter loci
#only keep loci if 80% missing, remove loci if >80% missing
filtered_samples.2 <- filtered_samples.1[,which(colMeans(!is.na(filtered_samples.1)) > 0.2)]
removed_samples.2 <- removed_samples.1[,which(colMeans(!is.na(removed_samples.1)) < 0.2)]


#export list of individuals that made the threshold
filtered_inds<-dplyr::select(filtered_samples.2, chr_pos)
write.csv(filtered_inds, "filtered_inds.csv", quote = F, row.names = F)

#export samples removed for too much missing data
write.csv(removed_samples.2,"removed_missing_data.csv", quote = F, row.names = F)

```

```{r}

#add comma to loci names and remove comma from last locus name
names(filtered_samples.2)<-gsub("$",",",names(filtered_samples.2))
# may need to change this line according to what the name of the last locus is in the filtered samples.2 file
names(filtered_samples.2)[length(names(filtered_samples.2))]<-"NW_0246098321_210707"

#add title and pop rows
title<-"title"
loci<- colnames(filtered_samples.2)
pop<-"pop"
#merge all new rows
meta.2<-rbind(title,loci, pop)
#set metadata column names to match the genotype column names to allow for merges
colnames(meta.2)<-colnames(filtered_samples.2)

#merge new metadata rows to dataset
genot.3<-rbind(meta.2,filtered_samples.2)

#add comma to Individual Name column
genot.3$inds<-sub("$",",",genot.3$chr_pos)

#remove extra "title" and "pop"s. also remove "inds," from loci row
genot.3[genot.3 == "title"] <- ""
genot.3[genot.3 == "pop"] <- ""
genot.3[genot.3 == "inds,,"] <- ""

#remove commas from title and pop
genot.3[genot.3 == "title,"] <- "title"
genot.3[genot.3 == "pop,"] <- "pop"

#export genepop file, open in text editor and remove first blank tab of loci row and resave
write.table(genot.3, "/Users/erincollins/Google Drive/My Drive/Erin's Projects/Chipps_DAPC/chipps_input_hatcheries.gen", sep = "\t", col.names = F, row.names = T, quote = F)

```



```{r}
#run with k=3, for fall, spring, yuba

x<-df2genind(filtered_samples.2, NA.char = NA, ploidy = 1)
# n.pca keeps all pcs, max.n.clust compares k1-k10, n.iter does 25 iterations, scale divides each mean value by standard deviation
grp<-find.clusters(x, n.pca = 200, max.n.clust = 10, n.iter = 25, scale = TRUE)
#to export a table with means for each k
write.csv(grp$Kstat, "kstats3_hatchery.csv")
#look at steps below to determine most descriptive k

#to export a table with assigned cluster for each individual based on selected k value
#this means may have to rerun and change the k value selected before exporting after best k is decided
write.csv(grp$grp, "/Users/erincollins/Google Drive/My Drive/Erin's Projects/Chipps_DAPC/clust_assign3_hatcheries.csv")

# run dapc to see clusters
dapc3 <- dapc(x, grp$grp)

#export dapc plot
pdf("dapc3springonly.pdf", width=8, height=8)
scatter(dapc3)
dev.off()

#export file to see which inds are in which cluster
write.csv(dapc3$grp, "dapc3_springonly.csv")

```

```{r}
### pca of populations in R for all markers

library(adegenet)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(tidyverse)

#remove column of ind, so they are not included as loci in the genind format
filtered_samples.3 <- dplyr::select(filtered_samples.2, -"chr_pos,")

#create genind format
x<-df2genind(filtered_samples.3, NA.char = NA, ploidy = 1)
#Import sample metadatas
meta <- read.csv("/Users/erincollins/Google Drive/My Drive/Erin's Projects/Chipps_DAPC/chipps_metadata.csv", header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors = F, colClasses = "character")
head(meta)

#to replace 0s with mean values
x1 <- scaleGen(x, NA.method="mean")
# do PCA analysis
ca1 <- dudi.pca(x1,scannf=F,nf=3)
#ca1$li are the row coordinates i.e. the principal components
#ca1$eig are the eigenvalues

#plot eigenvalues
pdf("pca_eigenvalues_springonly.pdf", width=8, height=8)
barplot(ca1$eig, main="eigenvalues", col=heat.colors(length(ca1$eig)), ylim=c(0,max(ceiling(ca1$eig))))
box()
dev.off()
  
#calculate % variation explained by each PC axis 
ev = ca1$eig/sum(ca1$eig)*100 

#import PCA scores and join sample metadata to scores
scores <- as.data.frame(ca1$li)
inds <- dplyr::select(filtered_inds, chr_pos)
scores$inds <- inds$chr_pos
scores <- dplyr::left_join(scores, meta, by = "inds")


#add variable for plotting symbols to scores
scores$pch = scores$population
scores$pch = as.character(scores$pch)
scores$pch[grepl("Fall", scores$pch)] = "21"
scores$pch[grepl("LateFall", scores$pch)] = "21"
scores$pch[grepl("WildSpring_MillDeer", scores$pch)] = "22"
scores$pch[grepl("WildSpring_Butte", scores$pch)] = "22"
scores$pch[grepl("Winter", scores$pch)] = "24"
scores$pch[grepl("Fall_Hatchery", scores$pch)] = "21"
scores$pch[grepl("Spring_Hatchery", scores$pch)] = "22"
scores$pch = as.integer(scores$pch)

leg.prep<-dplyr::select(scores, population, pch)
leg.prep<-unique(leg.prep)
#need to arrange alphabetically to match data colors and shapes to the legend colors and shapes
leg.prep <- dplyr::arrange(leg.prep, population)
leg.title = "Populations"
# this line is getting the color palette ready, turbo is the color palette, and the n= is just getting the number of colors based on the number of populations
pal = viridis::turbo(n=(length(leg.prep$population)))
# used the line below for spring only and specified the same colors as the plot with all pops
#pal = c("#9AFB40", "#FE9F2F")
leg.labs = leg.prep
leg.pch = leg.prep$pch


# PCA plot axes 1v2
pdf("pca_1v2_labels_hatchery.pdf", width = 12, height = 8)
print(ggplot(scores, aes(x=Axis1, y=Axis2)) + 
        geom_point(size=6, alpha=0.85, pch=scores$pch, color="black", aes(fill=population)) + 
        scale_fill_manual(name=leg.title, values=pal, labels=leg.labs) +
        labs(x=paste0("PC1 ", round(ev[1], 2), "%"), y=paste0("PC2 ", round(ev[2], 2), "%"), 
             title="Chipps Island juveniles 1996-2018: PCA Axes 1v2 ") +
        theme(axis.text=element_text(size=16), axis.title=element_text(size=18), plot.title=element_text(size=20)) +
        guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = leg.pch, size = 5), ncol=1))
#this line adds labels to each point, it looks messy, but can turn on to make sure legend is correct  
      #+ geom_text(label=scores$population, size=1.5)
      # this removes the gray background
      + theme_bw()
      )
dev.off()


  # PCA plot axes 1v3
pdf("pca_1v3_labels_hatchery.pdf", width = 12, height = 8)
print(ggplot(scores, aes(x=Axis1, y=Axis3)) + 
        geom_point(size=6, alpha=0.85, pch=scores$pch, color="black", aes(fill=population)) + 
        scale_fill_manual(name=leg.title, values=pal, labels=leg.labs) +
        labs(x=paste0("PC1 ", round(ev[1], 2), "%"), y=paste0("PC3 ", round(ev[3], 2), "%"), 
             title="Chipps Island juveniles 1996-2018: PCA Axes 1v3 ") +
        theme(axis.text=element_text(size=16), axis.title=element_text(size=18), plot.title=element_text(size=20)) +
        guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = leg.pch, size = 5), ncol=1))
      #+ geom_text(label=scores$population, size=1.5)
      + theme_bw()
      )
dev.off()

```


```{r}

# parse and create PCAs by years #

filtered_samples.4 <- dplyr::rename(filtered_samples.2, "inds" = "chr_pos,")
filtered_samples.4 <- dplyr::left_join(filtered_samples.4, meta, by = "inds")
filtered_samples.1.1996.2004 <- dplyr::filter(filtered_samples.4, SampleYear<2005)
filtered_samples.1.2007.2011 <- dplyr::filter(filtered_samples.4, SampleYear>2006 & SampleYear<2012)
filtered_samples.1.2015.2018 <- dplyr::filter(filtered_samples.4, SampleYear>2014)

#remove column of ind, so they are not included as loci in the genind format
filtered_samples1996.2004 <- dplyr::select(filtered_samples1996.2004, -"inds", -"SampleID", -"population", -"SampleYear")
filtered_samples2007.2011 <- dplyr::select(filtered_samples2007.2011, -"inds", -"SampleID", -"population", -"SampleYear")
filtered_samples2015.2018 <- dplyr::select(filtered_samples2015.2018, -"inds", -"SampleID", -"population", -"SampleYear")

#create genind format
x1996.2004<-df2genind(filtered_samples1996.2004, NA.char = NA, ploidy = 1)
x2007.2011<-df2genind(filtered_samples2007.2011, NA.char = NA, ploidy = 1)
x2015.2018<-df2genind(filtered_samples2015.2018, NA.char = NA, ploidy = 1)
#to replace 0s with mean values
x1.1996.2004 <- scaleGen(x1996.2004, NA.method="mean")
x1.2007.2011 <- scaleGen(x2007.2011, NA.method="mean")
x1.2015.2018 <- scaleGen(x2015.2018, NA.method="mean")

# do PCA analysis
ca1.1996.2004 <- dudi.pca(x1.1996.2004,scannf=F,nf=3)
ca1.2007.2011 <- dudi.pca(x1.2007.2011,scannf=F,nf=3)
ca1.2015.2018 <- dudi.pca(x1.2015.2018,scannf=F,nf=3)
#ca1$li are the row coordinates i.e. the principal components
#ca1$eig are the eigenvalues

#import PCA scores and join sample metadata to scores

inds1996.2004 <- dplyr::select(filtered_samples.1.1996.2004, inds)
inds2007.2011 <- dplyr::select(filtered_samples.1.2007.2011, inds)

scores1996.2004$inds <- inds1996.2004$inds
scores2007.2011$inds <- inds2007.2011$inds
scores2015.2018$inds <- inds2015.2018$inds

#add variable for plotting symbols to scores
scores1996.2004$pch = scores1996.2004$population
scores1996.2004$pch = as.character(scores1996.2004$pch)
scores1996.2004$pch[grepl("Fall", scores1996.2004$pch)] = "21"
scores1996.2004$pch[grepl("LateFall", scores1996.2004$pch)] = "21"
scores1996.2004$pch[grepl("WildSpring_MillDeer", scores1996.2004$pch)] = "22"
scores1996.2004$pch[grepl("WildSpring_Butte", scores1996.2004$pch)] = "22"
scores1996.2004$pch[grepl("Winter", scores1996.2004$pch)] = "24"
scores1996.2004$pch = as.integer(scores1996.2004$pch)

scores2007.2011$pch = scores2007.2011$population
scores2007.2011$pch = as.character(scores2007.2011$pch)
scores2007.2011$pch[grepl("Fall", scores2007.2011$pch)] = "21"
scores2007.2011$pch[grepl("LateFall", scores2007.2011$pch)] = "21"
scores2007.2011$pch[grepl("WildSpring_MillDeer", scores2007.2011$pch)] = "22"
scores2007.2011$pch[grepl("WildSpring_Butte", scores2007.2011$pch)] = "22"

scores2015.2018$pch[grepl("LateFall", scores2015.2018$pch)] = "21"
scores2015.2018$pch[grepl("WildSpring_MillDeer", scores2015.2018$pch)] = "22"
scores2015.2018$pch[grepl("WildSpring_Butte", scores2015.2018$pch)] = "22"

        geom_point(size=6, alpha=0.85, pch=scores2015.2018$pch, color="black", aes(fill=population)) + 
        scale_fill_manual(name=leg.title2015.2018, values=pal2015.2018, labels=leg.labs2015.2018) +
        labs(x=paste0("PC1 ", round(ev[1], 2), "%"), y=paste0("PC2 ", round(ev[2], 2), "%"), 
             title="Chipps Island juveniles 2015-2018: PCA Axes 1v2 ") +
        theme(axis.text=element_text(size=16), axis.title=element_text(size=18), plot.title=element_text(size=20)) +
        guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = leg.pch2015.2018, size = 5), ncol=1))
      #this line adds labels to each point, it looks messy, but can turn on to make sure legend is correct  
      #+ geom_text(label=scores2015.2018$population, size=1.5)
      # this removes the gray background
      + theme_bw()
      )
dev.off()

```

#no title row, just data
#no spaces or periods in names or in population names
#no indels, change - to 0

#Column 1 = Pedigree
#Column 2 = Individual ID
#Column 3 = Father ID, 0 if unknown
#Column 4 = Mother ID, 0 if unknown
#Column 5 = Sex, 1=M,XY, 2=F,XX, 0=Unknown and 0=YY
#Column 6 = Affected, 0 if unknown, 1 if unaffected, and 2 if affected
#			This can also represent phenotype data (maybe this is what affected means?)
#			Coded Winter/Spring=1, Summer=2, Unknown=0

#install.packages(c("fields","RColorBrewer","mapplots"))

   # install.packages("BiocManager")

source("http://membres-timc.imag.fr/Olivier.Francois/Conversion.R")
source("http://membres-timc.imag.fr/Olivier.Francois/POPSutilities.R")
library(LEA)

# to load a previously used project
#project = load.snmfProject("filtered.snmfProject")

# prep to format without filtering loci because they were causing an error, maybe odd number of loci
filtered_samples.5 <- dplyr::rename(filtered_samples.1, "inds"="chr_pos")
filtered_samples.5 <- dplyr::left_join(filtered_samples.5, meta, by = "inds")
# sort the filtered_samples by population column
filtered_samples.5 <- dplyr::arrange(filtered_samples.5, population)
filtered_samples.5 <- dplyr::select(filtered_samples.5, -"SampleID", -"population", -"SampleYear") 

# Convert to .ped format #
#Father and Mother ID, but just add 0s if unknown
filtered_samples.6<-add_column(filtered_samples.5, Pedigree = "Chipps", .before = "inds")
filtered_samples.6<-add_column(filtered_samples.6, FatherID = 0, .after = "inds")
filtered_samples.6<-add_column(filtered_samples.6, MotherID = 0, .after = "FatherID")
filtered_samples.6<-add_column(filtered_samples.6, Sex = 0, .after = "MotherID")
filtered_samples.6<-add_column(filtered_samples.6, Affected = 0, .after = "Sex")
#replace NA with 0
filtered_samples.6[is.na(filtered_samples.6)]<-0
#export .ped file
write.table(filtered_samples.6, "filtered.ped", sep = "\t", quote = F, row.names = F, col.names = F)



# ## ## WARNING: this will fail if header row is included #####
# ## ## other potential reason for failing, used filtered loci, which left an uneven number of loci ####
ped2geno("filtered.ped", force = TRUE)
#analysis to find k
obj.snmf = snmf("./filtered.geno", K = 1:6, ploidy = 2, entropy = T, repetitions = 25, CPU = 1, project = "new")



#plot k
plot(obj.snmf, col = "blue4", cex = 1.4, pch = 19)


##### admix 3 ####

#admixture analysis with k of 3 based on dip in plot
obj.snmf.3 = snmf("./filtered.geno", K = 3, alpha = 100, project = "new")
qmatrix.3 = Q(obj.snmf.3, K = 3)

#to plot admixture - rerun this chunk only when rearranging colors
tiff("/Users/erincollins/Google Drive/My Drive/Erin's Projects/Chipps_DAPC/admixplot3.tiff", height = 20, width = 40, units = 'cm', compression = "lzw", res = 500)
barplot(t(qmatrix.3), col = c("blue","purple","green"), border = NA, space = 0, xlab = "Individuals", ylab = "Admixture coefficients")
dev.off()

# check this file to get the order of populations, then can arrange the colors accordingly in the next chunk of code that plots these data
# get the admixture coefficient matrix, Q, for the 1st run for K = 3. 
res.3 = Q(obj.snmf.3, K = 3, run = 1)
write.csv(res.3,file = "admix_inds3.csv")
